newsitem.title: UK: BAA set to land higher half-year profits.
newsitem.headline: BAA set to land higher half-year profits.

text.p: British airports operator BAA Plc is expected to show a steady climb in profits when it reports half-year results on Monday.
Pretax profits are expected to rise to between 303 and 320 million stg for the six months to September 30 and the interim dividend to be increased to 4.6 pence a share from 4.125 pence.

Last month BAA's airline charges at its three London airports were pegged for the next five years by its regulator the Civil Aviation Authority, following a lengthy review which had dogged the share price for much of this year.

The review was regarded by analysts as relatively lenient but they say they now want to see how BAA is getting on with trying to get passengers to spend more in the bright new shopping arcades BAA has built at most of its seven British airports.
Retail income from its newly expanded empire of airport shopping arcades was up 10.5 percent last year at 556 million stg making airport shopping BAA's biggest single earner.
In comparison regulated landing and passenger handling charges brought in 360 million stg, accounting for 28 percent of last year's total group turnover of 1.25 billion stg.
